Exclusions: No implementation exists or is authorized. Federation/foundation plans examined only for cited decisions. PR81 merge and earlier implementer conduct are not scored. No other reviewer/probe was launched.

Exact source/store and hygiene checks are substantially accurate, but multiple observable failures remain in core recovery, audit, live-output and grading paths. Completeness is reduced by missing transition, response, artifact-worker and phase-binding contracts. MandatoryAttackSurfaces.Evidence: Four-phase ordering and explicit approval/freeze/gates pass. Artifact repair context, amended grade execution and exact production-acceptance dependencies are not decision-complete.

Claims.Evidence: The 33 S quotations were checked against the 55 genuine user messages extracted from the cited Cline session and the named handoff/profile sources; the seven P rules and D-01/D-02/D-05/D-06 rationale have sources. D-04/D-07/D-08 match the operator answers; D-03 correctly remains approval-owned. Literal carriage passes. Operational application fails for complete reviewer audit (F06), live output (F01), notification delivery (F02), remediation detail (F11), and verdict semantics (F13). D-08 UTC storage/identifier and local-display rules are applied in section 12 and the named identifier formats.

The document contains 94 Mermaid blocks, 65 flowcharts, 17 sequences, UC-HV-01 through UC-HV-12, and grouped relationship diagrams. This inventory does not establish complete contracts. Missing run-start ownership, incompatible amended grade input/guards, response finding shape, removal fields, cancel status, probe failure branch, and the overlength plugin key make the definitions non-executable as written. Nested diagrams exist but several omit required decision paths.

Durable queue, fenced writes, conditional claim, transactional finalization/outbox, replay, and at-least-once execution are sound stated patterns. W-01/02/04/05/06/07/08/09/11 have stated recovery and named catalog cases, but those labels do not prove all interleavings. W-03 assumes process death that the reused spawner does not guarantee; W-10 loses cancellation; W-12/audit hard stop has the triage write exception. Probe races and a late failure can invalidate readiness or undo completion. I-03/I-04/I-10/I-12 therefore lack a consistent implementation contract, and UC-HV-07 overclaims exactly-once delivery. I-09 prohibits TODO mutation and I-13 preserves the ledger; those policies themselves pass. P-02 does not prohibit intentional cancel, fencing, audit-failure or root-exit cleanup; no review deadline is needed for the fixes.

The current one-shot implementation does wait for process completion before yielding, confirming P8. The proposed adapter is explicitly line-live, and FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC003 is a good discriminating one-line-then-block test. The specified StreamReviewerOutput activity nevertheless cannot flush that single line on a timer without another line or exit; the end-to-end claim fails its own criterion.

S-29, R-19/R-20 and I-13 explicitly preserve the append-only ledger and indefinite evidence retention until explicit removal. No audit purge is authorized. All new entity mutations are intended to use AuditLedgerGuard. The actual FileHvIncident ordering permits an external write before that guard, and removal/read contracts are incomplete. These are executable gaps, not an objection to the stated retention policy.

All 78 probe files match the supplied manifest by length and SHA-256. Current versions/help were read without launching another review: Codex 0.162.1, Claude 2.1.300, Cline 3.0.71, Grok 1.0.60, Copilot 1.0.98. VI-01/02/03/04/06/07/08 and the qualified adapter statements match the receipts, including unproven Claude/Cline barriers, absent Cline runtime effort, Copilot model dependency, Grok max rejection, row-Id ordering, and the .NET multi-member gzip result. VI-05 asserts a false interval-imposed maximum despite byte-triggered flushes.

The foundation at base and HEAD hashes to 6E5D4F418E78CF9A76AB366F64D4F24002C09E3C3F024502ED89D77C6E77295E, matching the amendment. The document is unchanged from develop 36783b79. A-01 through A-12 identify the intended changes, but A-05 leaves the old Open-request guard, receipt-bearing DTO and pre-write procedure while calling the unit inside Finalizing. The overall response-verdict rule is also unreconciled; A-09 cites the wrong section for check 7. Thus they are not a complete, consistent replacement of the manual configured-grader clauses.

Exact store/catalog comparison passes: 21 FR, 21 TR, 21 TEST records, all pending; 114 distinct FR behavior criteria, each with named tests; the TEST projections repeat those 114 criteria and each TR has its catalog criterion. Titles, descriptions, criterion ids/text and 21 mapping groups (42 directed edges) match; every mapping edge has its TEST coverage statement. Equality does not make the behavior provable: response closure and removal criteria conflict with their units, and several necessary concurrency/crash criteria are absent. The complete real-binding phase allocation is not proven (U02). No product tests were executed or represented as passing.

P2 through P15 match the cited source behavior and evidence, with code in the review tree equal to base. P1 correctly identifies an unregistered worker but falsely describes criterion 4 as satisfied. Both TODOs carry the problem assignments, but the P1-P3 artifact-worker implementation contract is absent. Six PR81 comments were posted in review 5554472359 at 2026-10-16T22:48:12Z, after merge at 22:41:48Z; their six subjects match P10-P15. Federation D5/D7 require maintenance rekey and no dual-key lookup; foundation A7 requires blocking rather than auto-closing. FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005 is planned by that approved TODO and absent from the current store, as the amendment says. D-07 assigns all six fixes to this plan without adopting the two conflicting Codex remedies.

PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001 faithfully derives its principal phases and gates from section 20, is high priority, NOT APPROVED and unfinished, and explicitly preserves code freeze, operator approval, independent operator-named HV, Nuke gates with zero failures/skips and the four-phase requirements/interfaces-and-stubs/mock-TDD/implementation order. No implementation is authorized. It nevertheless inherits the incompatible finalization contract and leaves its promised artifact repairs without their units/tests. H1 versus later real-host/live-stream acceptance and H5/H6 activation remain unproven (U02). An accurate projection of an incomplete architecture is not an executable plan.

Section 20.2 explicitly runs build, test and deployment through Nuke, releases through Octopus, and excludes GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines from gates. H0/H1 and adapter/plugin design use PowerShell for scripts; C# product commands are not scripts. Integration/live reviewer checks use a separate temporary server, never the shared live server. Read-only store queries for this review are not integration tests. No defect found in this process ruling.

SPDX Apache-2.0 header, zero en/em dash characters, and zero Markdown tables pass. All nine effort commits change only the amendment and carry the required ClaudeCode model/effort/confidence signature. Scans of each reviewed document version, commit message and both plugin-read TODOs found no current marker credential or API-key literal. Local/remote HEAD match. Findings.Title: The output activity has no independent flush timer
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The live flush prose promises a maximum interval, but StreamReviewerOutput only tests that interval after a new line (amendment 1395, 1425-1437). A small line followed by silence never triggers an append. FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC001 and AC003 reject this trace. The activity and sequence need a timer-triggered flush independently of line arrival.

Findings.Title: Notification cursor, inbox and delivery are not crash-consistent
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: WatchHvNotifications persists its cursor and inbox in two files (1471), while its diagram claims one atomic replacement (1480). A crash after cursor advancement loses the notification. A fast completion can also be consumed before SubmitHvFromPlugin records its returned request in submitted (1453, 1461), then permanently ignored. UC-HV-07 (2200) promises exactly-once model delivery, contrary to the at-least-once rule and with no atomic delivery acknowledgment. The design needs a single recoverable cursor/inbox state and submission reconciliation, explicit deduplication and honest delivery guarantees, plus crash and fast-completion criteria.

Findings.Title: Configuration changes do not schedule the promised NONCE
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: UpdateHvReviewerCommand promises automatic NONCE after a configuration change (632), but HvWorkerHost requests NONCE only at startup (1372-1389). The claim path consumes only ProbeRequestedUtc (941), which update does not set. The promise needs a durable configuration-change probe request and polling/restart coverage.

Findings.Title: An old probe can qualify a new reviewer configuration
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A probe started for configuration A can finish after PATCH changes the reviewer to configuration B, then CloseHvRunOutputCommand unconditionally marks B Online (632, 1016). No captured reviewer configuration version exists on HvRun (484-490), nor does the probe close compare one. Readiness must bind to the configuration actually probed; add a stale-probe race criterion.

Findings.Title: Probe failures enter a request-only retry policy
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: FailHvRunCommand always calls the review-request-only HvRetryDecision (1045-1067, 1346), although a Probe has no HvRequestId (484) and a failed launch or nonzero probe exit uses this same command (1395). The probe failure and shutdown outcomes require an explicit branch, with offline/incident and retry semantics tested.

Findings.Title: Reviewer-turn verification accepts an incomplete or open audit turn
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: V-6 accepts a reviewer turn containing only the compact hv_verdict (1283, 553). It does not require the entire result or a closed Chore turn, as P-06 and the brief require (544). A persisted summary-only or open turn can pass finalization. Verification and negative criteria must check the complete result and required terminal state.

Findings.Title: The stored result contains its own unspecified content hash
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: HvEvidence stores the result document with only responseLog removed (494), while that document contains evidence.result.sha256 (562), and its Sha256 hashes the decompressed stored bytes (494). No exclusion/projection defines a hashable payload without its own hash. Define one canonical stored payload and add its digest to the returned envelope, with a named hash/round-trip case.

Findings.Title: Incident filing writes before the audit hard-stop guard
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: FileHvIncidentCommand calls the writing triage service before AuditLedgerGuard (1156, 1163-1171), contrary to the hard-stop rule that no HV unit writes while the ledger is unavailable (369, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-018-AC002). Its diagram also puts Filed and notification writes after an edge labeled committed. The guard and audited triage write need an enforceable ordering/transaction boundary, and the diagram must put local outcome and notification inside the transaction.

Findings.Title: P1 misstates the live requirement satisfaction flag
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: P1 states that FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4 is satisfied (amendment 2509; REMED-HVPIPELINE-001 P1). The live requirement read has isSatisfied false (hv-r1-related-requirements.json:82-84). Correct the factual claim in both artifacts, retaining the independently verified missing-worker defect. Do not change the store to fit the claim.

Findings.Title: The retained model-grade contract cannot execute inside finalization
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A-05 leaves the foundation model-grade input and guards incompatible with its new caller (amendment 183, 1100, 1178; foundation 3383, 3386, 3410, 3426, 3445). The request must be Open in the retained foundation contract, but finalization calls it while Finalizing. The old DTO still requires removed receipt paths and thread fields; its pre-write staleness dispatch expects no transaction, whereas the new call is inside one. Replace the complete internal grade contract, guards, side effects, and diagrams, including responsibility for completing the outer request. A-09 also names section 3.1 for a check actually in 6.3 (foundation 2842).

Findings.Title: Response findings cannot satisfy or survive the result contract
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The response finding wire shape (551) has only claimId, check, outcome, whereas V-8 (1285) requires category, location, evidence and remediation on every finding. HvFinding (498) has no response scope or response id, and the result's responseGrades omit findings (562) while its failures promise every FAIL and UNKNOWN (564). Define a lossless response finding contract and result projection, with negative tests for missing remediation and positive failing-grade persistence.

Findings.Title: A legitimate mid-review response closure invalidates the reviewer
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: ResponseStatusTransition may close a Pending response during review (182, 480; FR-MCP-HVPIPE-021-AC003), while the accepted request is immutable (544). V-3/V-8 bind against the current Pending set (1280, 1285). A reviewer legitimately grading the admitted response after it closes is rejected and taken Offline. Bind reviewer output to the accepted set and define how closed items are ignored at commit, with reject/supersede races covered.

Findings.Title: Overall verdict predicates contradict one another
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: V-4 makes overall AGREE an iff over holistic and turn verdicts, omitting response grades (1281), while importing the foundation verdict_match iff over response grades (foundation 2840). These rules disagree for mixed turn/response outcomes and R-31 forbids every FAIL/UNKNOWN (173). Define one overall predicate over all applicable verdicts and findings and propagate it to the foundation replacement and criteria.

Findings.Title: No command owns the run-start state and metadata
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: No unit persists HvRun StartedUtc, ProcessId or the Claimed-to-Running transition. The run declares these fields (486), V-6 and ReadinessProbeVerdict use StartedUtc, Claim only starts the request (941), heartbeat only renews it (971), and RunReviewerProcess starts the OS process without a fenced run-start write (1395-1405). Define the owning command and its ordering/crash outcomes, with start/provenance tests.

Findings.Title: Successful output close can discard an accepted cancellation
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: Cancel can commit CancelRequested after the last heartbeat and before successful process exit; CloseHvRunOutputCommand then overwrites it with Finalizing without checking cancellation (1016). This loses an accepted cancellation. R-28 also refuses repeat cancel of Canceled (170), while CancelHvRequestCommand returns 200 for it (787). Define consistent repeat semantics and the serialized cancel/close/finalize outcomes, with each interleaving tested.

Findings.Title: Evidence removal leaves entity fields and read outcomes undefined
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: RemoveHvEvidenceCommand writes RemovedBy and RemovalReason to output chunks (859, 873), but their entity has neither field (492). GetHvRequestQuery's lastOutput and StreamHvRunOutputQuery still decompress removed payloads without a removed-evidence outcome (753, 880-893), unlike FR-MCP-HVPIPE-019-AC004. Define the retained fields and post-removal behavior on every payload-reading surface, with named cases.

Findings.Title: VI-05 understates the possible append rate
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: VI-05's asserted maximum of 14400 appends per run hour (2500) is false under R-12 and the byte-triggered flush (1395): multiple OutputFlushBytes batches can arrive within one interval. State a valid measurement workload and account for byte-triggered writes and audit overhead; do not call this an interval-imposed bound.

Findings.Title: The artifact-worker repair has no contract for its existing requirements
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: H3 promises P1 to P3 fixed using HvWorkerHost (167, 2486), but the host and claim/failure/finalization contracts only service HvRequest. The live FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 AC4 separately requires configured/default AgentPool behavior, distinct request/attempt/pool-job/model-execution/accepted-result identities, internal-only cancellation and one accepted terminal result. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 AC4 prohibits raw artifact/prompt storage, unlike turn HV's complete brief log. No artifact queue adapter, units, identity mapping, retention boundary, or tests integrate these unchanged requirements. Define that separate-context contract and its H0 mocks/H3 production cases before approval, sharing only compatible execution primitives.

Findings.Title: Abrupt worker death has no guaranteed reviewer-process cleanup
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: W-03 and sequence 17.7 assume the reviewer process is gone when the worker crashes (298, 1870). The reused IProcessSpawner starts an ordinary process and provides explicit Kill only (DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51). A killed worker cannot call Kill or observe stale_fence; lease expiry fences database writes but does not stop its child. No owner-death containment or recovery outcome is specified. Define and test abrupt worker death with a surviving reviewer and descendants, without imposing a review deadline.

Findings.Title: Plugin idempotency keys exceed their limit and omit invocation identity
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The plugin idempotency key embeds the full requestId plus a fixed 20-character prefix/suffix overhead (1453), but requestId may be 256 and IdempotencyKey only 128 (453, 471). A valid requestId above 108 characters produces an invalid key. It also omits the full submitting session identity and contextFormat, although the payload fingerprint includes them. Define a bounded canonical key over the full invocation identity and test maximum-length and cross-session calls.

Findings.Title: A late verification failure can undo successful finalization
Findings.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A late verification failure can overwrite successful finalization. FailHvRunCommand accepts null WorkerId and the released stored fence (1045), checks only FencedLease, and writes Failed plus request retry state (1046). Finalize may commit Succeeded/Completed first (1100) without changing that released fence. Unlike finalization, Fail does not re-check OutputClosed/Finalizing and versions in its transaction. A finalizer that read the earlier state can therefore undo completion. Add state/version-conditional failure acceptance and idempotent terminal behavior, with a concurrent success/verification-failure test.

Unknowns.Title: No-force push flags are not proven
Unknowns.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: Nine signed effort commits and eight adjacent recorded push transitions are verified linear and fast-forward. A reflog's update-by-push message does not prove which flags were used. The absolute claim that every push used no force flag needs the original push command/output or a server audit. Do not invent that evidence.

Unknowns.Title: Real acceptance-test phase ownership is incomplete
Unknowns.DefectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The catalog has named tests for all 114 FR acceptance criteria, but no complete real-binding AC-to-phase allocation is supplied. In particular, H1 owns live reviewer/plugin qualification while the worker arrives H3 and streams H6; H5 watcher and H6 stream delivery are parallel, with no explicit activation/rollback contract. Component mocks can be correct, but they do not prove that these production acceptance cases can run in the owning phase. Provide the exact phase and prerequisite binding for each criterion and distinguish H1 adapter tests from later server-launched/live-stream cases. This is an evidence/plan edit, not a request to lower or waive a gate.

failList.title: The output activity has no independent flush timer
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The live flush prose promises a maximum interval, but StreamReviewerOutput only tests that interval after a new line (amendment 1395, 1425-1437). A small line followed by silence never triggers an append. FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008-AC001 and AC003 reject this trace. The activity and sequence need a timer-triggered flush independently of line arrival.

failList.title: Notification cursor, inbox and delivery are not crash-consistent
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: WatchHvNotifications persists its cursor and inbox in two files (1471), while its diagram claims one atomic replacement (1480). A crash after cursor advancement loses the notification. A fast completion can also be consumed before SubmitHvFromPlugin records its returned request in submitted (1453, 1461), then permanently ignored. UC-HV-07 (2200) promises exactly-once model delivery, contrary to the at-least-once rule and with no atomic delivery acknowledgment. The design needs a single recoverable cursor/inbox state and submission reconciliation, explicit deduplication and honest delivery guarantees, plus crash and fast-completion criteria.

failList.title: Configuration changes do not schedule the promised NONCE
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: UpdateHvReviewerCommand promises automatic NONCE after a configuration change (632), but HvWorkerHost requests NONCE only at startup (1372-1389). The claim path consumes only ProbeRequestedUtc (941), which update does not set. The promise needs a durable configuration-change probe request and polling/restart coverage.

failList.title: An old probe can qualify a new reviewer configuration
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A probe started for configuration A can finish after PATCH changes the reviewer to configuration B, then CloseHvRunOutputCommand unconditionally marks B Online (632, 1016). No captured reviewer configuration version exists on HvRun (484-490), nor does the probe close compare one. Readiness must bind to the configuration actually probed; add a stale-probe race criterion.

failList.title: Probe failures enter a request-only retry policy
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: FailHvRunCommand always calls the review-request-only HvRetryDecision (1045-1067, 1346), although a Probe has no HvRequestId (484) and a failed launch or nonzero probe exit uses this same command (1395). The probe failure and shutdown outcomes require an explicit branch, with offline/incident and retry semantics tested.

failList.title: Reviewer-turn verification accepts an incomplete or open audit turn
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: V-6 accepts a reviewer turn containing only the compact hv_verdict (1283, 553). It does not require the entire result or a closed Chore turn, as P-06 and the brief require (544). A persisted summary-only or open turn can pass finalization. Verification and negative criteria must check the complete result and required terminal state.

failList.title: The stored result contains its own unspecified content hash
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: HvEvidence stores the result document with only responseLog removed (494), while that document contains evidence.result.sha256 (562), and its Sha256 hashes the decompressed stored bytes (494). No exclusion/projection defines a hashable payload without its own hash. Define one canonical stored payload and add its digest to the returned envelope, with a named hash/round-trip case.

failList.title: Incident filing writes before the audit hard-stop guard
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: FileHvIncidentCommand calls the writing triage service before AuditLedgerGuard (1156, 1163-1171), contrary to the hard-stop rule that no HV unit writes while the ledger is unavailable (369, FR-MCP-HVPIPE-018-AC002). Its diagram also puts Filed and notification writes after an edge labeled committed. The guard and audited triage write need an enforceable ordering/transaction boundary, and the diagram must put local outcome and notification inside the transaction.

failList.title: P1 misstates the live requirement satisfaction flag
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: P1 states that FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 criterion 4 is satisfied (amendment 2509; REMED-HVPIPELINE-001 P1). The live requirement read has isSatisfied false (hv-r1-related-requirements.json:82-84). Correct the factual claim in both artifacts, retaining the independently verified missing-worker defect. Do not change the store to fit the claim.

failList.title: The retained model-grade contract cannot execute inside finalization
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A-05 leaves the foundation model-grade input and guards incompatible with its new caller (amendment 183, 1100, 1178; foundation 3383, 3386, 3410, 3426, 3445). The request must be Open in the retained foundation contract, but finalization calls it while Finalizing. The old DTO still requires removed receipt paths and thread fields; its pre-write staleness dispatch expects no transaction, whereas the new call is inside one. Replace the complete internal grade contract, guards, side effects, and diagrams, including responsibility for completing the outer request. A-09 also names section 3.1 for a check actually in 6.3 (foundation 2842).

failList.title: Response findings cannot satisfy or survive the result contract
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The response finding wire shape (551) has only claimId, check, outcome, whereas V-8 (1285) requires category, location, evidence and remediation on every finding. HvFinding (498) has no response scope or response id, and the result's responseGrades omit findings (562) while its failures promise every FAIL and UNKNOWN (564). Define a lossless response finding contract and result projection, with negative tests for missing remediation and positive failing-grade persistence.

failList.title: A legitimate mid-review response closure invalidates the reviewer
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: ResponseStatusTransition may close a Pending response during review (182, 480; FR-MCP-HVPIPE-021-AC003), while the accepted request is immutable (544). V-3/V-8 bind against the current Pending set (1280, 1285). A reviewer legitimately grading the admitted response after it closes is rejected and taken Offline. Bind reviewer output to the accepted set and define how closed items are ignored at commit, with reject/supersede races covered.

failList.title: Overall verdict predicates contradict one another
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: V-4 makes overall AGREE an iff over holistic and turn verdicts, omitting response grades (1281), while importing the foundation verdict_match iff over response grades (foundation 2840). These rules disagree for mixed turn/response outcomes and R-31 forbids every FAIL/UNKNOWN (173). Define one overall predicate over all applicable verdicts and findings and propagate it to the foundation replacement and criteria.

failList.title: No command owns the run-start state and metadata
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: No unit persists HvRun StartedUtc, ProcessId or the Claimed-to-Running transition. The run declares these fields (486), V-6 and ReadinessProbeVerdict use StartedUtc, Claim only starts the request (941), heartbeat only renews it (971), and RunReviewerProcess starts the OS process without a fenced run-start write (1395-1405). Define the owning command and its ordering/crash outcomes, with start/provenance tests.

failList.title: Successful output close can discard an accepted cancellation
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: Cancel can commit CancelRequested after the last heartbeat and before successful process exit; CloseHvRunOutputCommand then overwrites it with Finalizing without checking cancellation (1016). This loses an accepted cancellation. R-28 also refuses repeat cancel of Canceled (170), while CancelHvRequestCommand returns 200 for it (787). Define consistent repeat semantics and the serialized cancel/close/finalize outcomes, with each interleaving tested.

failList.title: Evidence removal leaves entity fields and read outcomes undefined
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: RemoveHvEvidenceCommand writes RemovedBy and RemovalReason to output chunks (859, 873), but their entity has neither field (492). GetHvRequestQuery's lastOutput and StreamHvRunOutputQuery still decompress removed payloads without a removed-evidence outcome (753, 880-893), unlike FR-MCP-HVPIPE-019-AC004. Define the retained fields and post-removal behavior on every payload-reading surface, with named cases.

failList.title: VI-05 understates the possible append rate
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: VI-05's asserted maximum of 14400 appends per run hour (2500) is false under R-12 and the byte-triggered flush (1395): multiple OutputFlushBytes batches can arrive within one interval. State a valid measurement workload and account for byte-triggered writes and audit overhead; do not call this an interval-imposed bound.

failList.title: The artifact-worker repair has no contract for its existing requirements
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: H3 promises P1 to P3 fixed using HvWorkerHost (167, 2486), but the host and claim/failure/finalization contracts only service HvRequest. The live FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 AC4 separately requires configured/default AgentPool behavior, distinct request/attempt/pool-job/model-execution/accepted-result identities, internal-only cancellation and one accepted terminal result. FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-002 AC4 prohibits raw artifact/prompt storage, unlike turn HV's complete brief log. No artifact queue adapter, units, identity mapping, retention boundary, or tests integrate these unchanged requirements. Define that separate-context contract and its H0 mocks/H3 production cases before approval, sharing only compatible execution primitives.

failList.title: Abrupt worker death has no guaranteed reviewer-process cleanup
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: W-03 and sequence 17.7 assume the reviewer process is gone when the worker crashes (298, 1870). The reused IProcessSpawner starts an ordinary process and provides explicit Kill only (DefaultProcessSpawner.cs:12-16,48-51). A killed worker cannot call Kill or observe stale_fence; lease expiry fences database writes but does not stop its child. No owner-death containment or recovery outcome is specified. Define and test abrupt worker death with a surviving reviewer and descendants, without imposing a review deadline.

failList.title: Plugin idempotency keys exceed their limit and omit invocation identity
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: The plugin idempotency key embeds the full requestId plus a fixed 20-character prefix/suffix overhead (1453), but requestId may be 256 and IdempotencyKey only 128 (453, 471). A valid requestId above 108 characters produces an invalid key. It also omits the full submitting session identity and contextFormat, although the payload fingerprint includes them. Define a bounded canonical key over the full invocation identity and test maximum-length and cross-session calls.

failList.title: A late verification failure can undo successful finalization
failList.defectEvidenceAndRequiredChange: A late verification failure can overwrite successful finalization. FailHvRunCommand accepts null WorkerId and the released stored fence (1045), checks only FencedLease, and writes Failed plus request retry state (1046). Finalize may commit Succeeded/Completed first (1100) without changing that released fence. Unlike finalization, Fail does not re-check OutputClosed/Finalizing and versions in its transaction. A finalizer that read the earlier state can therefore undo completion. Add state/version-conditional failure acceptance and idempotent terminal behavior, with a concurrent success/verification-failure test.

unknownList.title: No-force push flags are not proven
unknownList.evidenceAndRequiredChange: Nine signed effort commits and eight adjacent recorded push transitions are verified linear and fast-forward. A reflog's update-by-push message does not prove which flags were used. The absolute claim that every push used no force flag needs the original push command/output or a server audit. Do not invent that evidence.

unknownList.title: Real acceptance-test phase ownership is incomplete
unknownList.evidenceAndRequiredChange: The catalog has named tests for all 114 FR acceptance criteria, but no complete real-binding AC-to-phase allocation is supplied. In particular, H1 owns live reviewer/plugin qualification while the worker arrives H3 and streams H6; H5 watcher and H6 stream delivery are parallel, with no explicit activation/rollback contract. Component mocks can be correct, but they do not prove that these production acceptance cases can run in the owning phase. Provide the exact phase and prerequisite binding for each criterion and distinguish H1 adapter tests from later server-launched/live-stream cases. This is an evidence/plan edit, not a request to lower or waive a gate.

FinalPersistenceProof.OrderVerification: Integer order values were submitted. The QueryAsync DTO omits order; exact content and explicit numbered headers are verified in the returned processingDialog sequence.
